key_insight: LEAP combines a domain-trained LLM with active learning to prioritize perovskite precursor additives using mechanism-aware, uncertainty-guided decisions.
engineering_relevance: This framework can reduce trial-and-error screening by focusing experiments on additives that are both literature-consistent and practically feasible for device fabrication.
method: Trains a specialized LLM to extract mechanism-relevant knowledge from perovskite additive literature.
Represents candidate molecules with interpretable descriptors and feeds them into Bayesian optimization.
Uses expert-in-the-loop feasibility review to refine additive prioritization across screening rounds.
evidence_signal: On unseen literature, the domain-specific model outperformed general-purpose models in mechanism-consistent reasoning, and later-round experimental devices reached average PCEs of 20.13% and 20.87% versus 19.25% for the control, with a champion PCE of 21.32%.
watch_item: The reported gains come from a proof-of-concept study, so broader validation is still needed to confirm robustness across different perovskite chemistries and experimental settings.
paper_title: LEAP: A closed-loop framework for perovskite precursor additive discovery
